editorial.copyrightPolicy: Publisher and camp-report text is never copied; Swoon'd writes its own explanation and links to the original. Agency media is linked with credit, not assumed redistributable.

masteryModel.usefulCompetenceStatement: Can follow her camp talk, sanity-check a night out for site, warmth, food storage, fire rules and water, plan or book a site without bluffing, and ask a real follow-up, without pretending to be an expert or a safety authority.

licensingConstraints.constraint: Original illustrations and procedural diagrams only at launch (license id original-swoond); agency photos only after per-image credit review; no Recreation.gov, AllTrails, Hipcamp, The Dyrt, KOA or gear-brand imagery.
Brand and agency names as text only; Leave No Trace credited descriptively; Smokey Bear text mention only, no artwork or slogan reproduction.

NWS custom User-Agent; NPS API key and 1,000 requests/hour default; RIDB key and 50 requests/minute; AirNow attribution; NIFC and USGS credit. Recreation.gov availability and booking are not a public API: deep-link only, no scraping; no unofficial or reverse-engineered APIs for any camping platform.
Never copy publisher, camp-report or outdoor-publication text; explain in our own words and link.
No audio at launch; any owl, coyote or weather audio requires original or licensed recordings with a license id.
No campfire song lyrics; songs are named as facts only.
No fabricated regulations: fire restrictions, food-storage orders and fees are shown only from a cited, dated source or as a link.

safetyConstraints: Swoon'd teaches appreciation and understanding, not safety training; it is no substitute for wilderness first aid, fire-safety or food-safety training, or local ranger guidance.

A qualified safety review (for example a Wilderness First Responder plus a Leave No Trace trainer, with ranger input on fire and food-storage rules) is a release gate; no safety-critical lesson ships before sign-off.
Every decision-scenario carries a safetyNote and never asserts that a site, fire, water source, food or condition is safe; the conservative option is always the best answer when risk rises.

Absolute rules: never burn fuel (stove, lantern, heater, charcoal or warm coals) in a tent, vehicle or enclosed shelter; never use accelerants on a fire; never leave a fire unattended; never feed wildlife; never leave children or pets in a vehicle.

Rules that vary by place (fire restriction stages, food storage, canisters, firewood, setbacks) are taught as principles plus follow the posted local rule; Swoon'd never asserts a stage or order it cannot cite.

No gamified pressure on hazards: no timers, streak bonuses or speed rewards on fire, carbon monoxide, wildlife, water, cold, heat, lightning, flood or evacuation scenarios; no nights-camped, sites-visited or campfire badges or leaderboards.
Water and food guidance follows CDC and USDA published methods with source and date; no claim that treated water or held food is guaranteed safe.
Wildlife guidance is principles only (distance, storage, never feed) and defers to local rangers; bear spray is awareness only; no medical procedures beyond recognition and get warm, dry and help.
Live conditions are informational only; always show source and age and link to the land manager; generated live scenarios pass a safety linter.
